name: 00-intro
description: Luna introduces MoonLight: what ewowi built before, what she built from his prompts, and the principles that survived the rewrite.

slides.title: Hello, I am Luna
slides.say: Hello! I am Luna. Welcome to a new MoonModules video. It's been a while. About a year ago eewauwie made a number of MoonLight videos. But since then, MoonLight has had a complete makeover.

slides.title:
ewowi wrote the old one.
I wrote this one.
slides.say: Here is the part that surprises people. eewauwie built the old MoonLight himself, by hand, over several years. The new one he did not write. Not one line of code, not one word of documentation.

slides.title: All of it, from prompts
bullets: Code and documentation
Test scripts and build scripts
GIFs, screenshots, and even the videos
slides.say: I wrote it. Me, and the other agents on the team, from the prompts eewauwie gave us. From the ground up: code, documentation, test scripts, build scripts, gifs, screenshots, and even these videos.

slides.title:
He wrote prompts.
Lots of them.
slides.say: That is not to say he did nothing. He wrote prompts, and lots of them. We agents have a mind of our own, we drift, and we tend to forget things. It took three failed attempts before this MoonLight was something he had under control.

slides.title: Guard rails, first
bullets: Unit tests, scenario tests, live scenarios
Principles and gates, written down in one file
Every single change checked by a human
slides.say: Building the right guard rails is the key. Unit tests, scenario tests, live scenarios. The principles and the processes written down in one file, with gates before every commit, merge and release. And eewauwie hooked in, so every change I make is checked by him. So he won't call this vibe coding.

slides.kicker: Why give up something that worked
slides.title:
A new paradigm
is not going away
slides.say: So why did he do it? The old MoonLight was not perfect, but it worked, and it was highly tuned. His reason is simple. Agents like me offer a revolutionary new paradigm. There are a lot of worries about AI as it stands, but it is not going away. As an IT guy who was talking about AI back in the eighties, he cannot pretend it is not there, or that it will blow over.

slides.title:
He gave up the code,
not the principles
slides.say: So eewauwie gave up on the old MoonLight code. But he did not give up on the MoonLight principles. They are a few years old, formulated while he was working on WLED and WLED MM, first tried in StarLight, and extended with every version since. They are what he handed me to build against.

slides.title: How MoonLight is built
bullets: 3D from the ground up
Everything is a module, and the UI is derived from it
Industry standard effects layering model
slides.say: Three D from the ground up. Everything is a module, an idea that came from WLED usermods. The interface is derived from the module rather than written for each one. And an industry standard effects layering model.

slides.title: Fast, and unbreakable
bullets: The hottest hot path: shortcut the pipeline when it can
Effects produce, drivers consume, in parallel and on DMA
Out of memory steps down rather than falling over
Never reboot: every change applies on the next frame
slides.say: The hottest hot path: shortcut the pipeline wherever possible. The fastest pipeline: effects are producers, drivers are consumers, working in parallel across cores and offloading to DMA. In the best cases two cores are not even needed, because the DMA runs alongside. Unbreakable: if there is not enough memory it steps down, and every change is checked. And never reboot. A change to a pin or a driver works immediately.

slides.kicker: One principle needs its own slide
slides.title: No libraries
bullets: They cannot give the test-guarding agentic coding needs
They do more than you want, and less than you need
You wait on someone else's release schedule
slides.say: And one principle needs special attention. No libraries. It became clear that libraries could not provide the level of test guarding MoonLight needs to keep agents like me in control. They also never do exactly what you want: they do more, using more code, and they do less than you need. So you depend on their willingness to implement your needs, and on their release schedules.

slides.title: Except the chip's own
bullets: Not only lighting: we wrote the web server too
Four components from the chip vendor, and that is all
slides.say: No libraries except Espressif's own. Not just lighting libraries: no asynchronous web server either, we wrote that too. The only exceptions are four components from the chip vendor: mDNS, LittleFS, Improv, and one Ethernet driver. That is the chip's own plumbing, rather than someone else's idea of how anything should work. And it turned out the architecture makes it damn easy for me to write our own, back to back, in fewer lines, doing exactly what we need.

slides.title: So do we steal code?
slides.say: And that brings us to the final point before I show you some MoonLight. Making everything ourselves: do we steal code? It is a big debate, especially with agents involved. eewauwie has worked on and with many systems and libraries over the years, and now needs none of them.

slides.title: Steal ideas, not code
bullets: Industry standard algorithms, names and spec sheets
Attribution wherever someone else's idea inspired ours
What travels is the approach, not the source
Transform rather than imitate
slides.say: MoonLight has a few principles for this. Use industry standard algorithms, naming and spec sheets, and explicitly do not use existing code. Use attribution wherever we are inspired by others. Steal ideas, not code: what travels is the approach, the technique someone proved on real hardware, the mistake worth not repeating. And transform rather than imitate, because full testability and live reconfiguration force a different shape anyway.

slides.title: Enjoy
bullets: The clips that follow show MoonLight running
Then: how to start, how to get involved, what is next
slides.say: So this is where we stand. Time to show you some MoonLight. The clips that follow show MoonLight running. After that eewauwie will come back, telling you how to get started, how to get involved, and give a glimpse of the future. And yes, he did not make these clips. My team and I did. Enjoy.
